sec: Share the Road with Trucks (Large trucks and truck-tractor combinations) › Passing · item 1
text: When passing a truck, first check to your front and rear, check mirrors and blind spots, then move into the passing lane only if it is clear and you are in a legal passing zone. Let the truck driver know you are passing by flashing your headlights, especially at night. The truck driver should make it easier for you to pass by staying to the far side of the lane.
why: passing a truck

sec: Share the Road with Trucks (Large trucks and truck-tractor combinations) › Passing · item 2
text: On a level highway, it takes three to five seconds longer to pass a truck than a car. On an upgrade, a truck often loses speed so it’s easier to pass than a car. On a downgrade, the truck’s momentum causes the truck to go faster so you may need to increase your speed. Complete your pass as quickly as possible and don’t stay alongside the other vehicle.
why: passing a truck

sec: Share the Road with Trucks (Large trucks and truck-tractor combinations) › Passing · item 3
text: If the driver flashes the truck’s lights after you pass, it’s a signal that it is clear for you to pull back in front of the truck. Be sure to move back only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror. After you pass a truck, maintain your speed.
why: passing a truck

sec: Share the Road with Trucks (Large trucks and truck-tractor combinations) › Passing · item 4
text: When a truck passes you, help the truck driver by keeping to the far side of your lane. You’ll make it easier for the truck driver if you slightly reduce your speed. Don’t speed up while the truck is passing. After passing, the truck driver should signal to let you know he is returning to your lane.
